label: Market Close
headline: S&P +2.35%, Nasdaq 100 +3.4%, chips +6.85%, WTI -4.4% to $86.85, 3y tail 0.5bp, Take-Two +4% AH
stance: The Hormuz trade reversed both ways Monday: oil to its lowest since August, S&P its best day in 7 months. Rates did not join; CPI at 8:30 decides whether they must.

scorecard.call: Morning: Nasdaq 100 futures flat pre-market, the rebound has not crossed the Pacific.
scorecard.actual: It crossed. Nasdaq 100 +3.4%, S&P +2.35% at the close, every sector higher, the S&P's biggest day since April 8.

scorecard.call: Morning: 3y auction 1pm; the 10y is 50bp off its peak into the supply.
scorecard.actual: Tailed 0.5bp at 4.627%, bid-to-cover 2.53, lowest since August 2025. Dealers left with 9.5%, directs a record 35%.

scorecard.call: Midday: the Qatar meeting at noon decides whether oil, and the rally, hold into CPI.
scorecard.actual: Trump after the meeting: war "effectively over", blockade stays. WTI settled $86.85, -4.4%; equities held to the close.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Trump, ~3pm ET: conflict with Iran "effectively over", no new strikes planned, blockade stays. Brent settled $92.57, -5.9%; WTI $86.85, -4.4%, lowest since August.
3y auction: 4.627%, a 0.5bp tail, bid-to-cover 2.53, lowest since August 2025. Indirects 55.5%, directs a record 35%, dealers 9.5%. 10y auction Tuesday 1pm.
Goolsbee and Barkin Monday: services inflation picking up, rates may need to go higher. December hike odds above 80% (~5:40pm ET).

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Chip index +6.85% at the close, about 10% above Thursday's close. Memory and optical names +6-16%; the one large chip name lower is a company story, not a sector one.
All 11 sectors higher at the close: industrials +3.8%, discretionary +3.1%, energy +0.4%. Energy was the laggard; AI dip buying led.
S&P futures little changed, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.2% (~6pm ET) into Tuesday's CPI. No fade after the close.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY ETF +0.4%, IG ETF +0.1% at the close against S&P +2.35%. Credit did not chase the equity rebound; Friday's HY widening is not yet unwound.

items.head: Take-Two +4% after hours (~6:45pm ET) on GTA VI preorders
items.body: Q2 bookings $1.60bn vs $1.58bn expected, EPS $0.99 vs $0.94. Preorders "far in excess" of expectations; the game launches next week. Closed -3.5%.

items.head: Rocket Lab -4.2% after hours: Neutron debut slips to 2027
items.body: Q3 revenue $267.8mn, +73%, above guidance; loss $0.12 vs $0.07 expected. Q4 guide $270-290mn vs $264.6mn. Closed +10.9% before the report.

items.head: Nvidia -4.3% to $178.67, lowest close since April 7
items.body: Board probe of Huang kept it the only large chip name lower while the chip index rose 6.85%. Reports Nov 17.

watch.head: CPI Tuesday Nov 10, 8:30
watch.body: Consensus headline +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%. First inflation read with December hike odds above 80%; the monthly core change is the number.

watch.head: 10y auction 1pm Tuesday, after the 3y tail
watch.body: Front end drew the lowest bid-to-cover since August 2025 Monday. Cash Treasuries closed Wednesday, so 10y Tuesday and 30y Thursday carry the week.

watch.head: CoreWeave reports Tuesday; SoftBank too
watch.body: CoreWeave +5.6% at the close ahead of the report. The debt-funded AI build gets its first read since the midterms.
